quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a danger of driving too fast?

options.text: It saves time getting to your destination.
It helps you avoid obstacles.
It increases the risk of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor decisions.

questions.question: What is an important step before turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle. Make sure it is safe to turn. Slow down to turn safely.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content and alcohol's effects.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive carefully and pay special attention in these areas.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When there is a solid line next to your lane.
When there is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers may cross it to change lanes. A solid line next to a broken line means only drivers in the lane with the broken line may pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Children on bikes may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: What does a stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if cars are approaching.
Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
Drive carefully through without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Stop completely at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that diverts your attention from driving. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas where your vision blurs when tired.
Areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder. Check the rear corners of your vehicle where your mirrors cannot see. These are called blind spots.

questions.question: How should you use a two-part safety belt?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt together. Using only one part gives you much less protection. Buckle both even if you have an automatic shoulder belt.

questions.question: What happens when you constantly pass other cars on a two-lane road?

options.text: You reach your destination much faster and safer.
You increase your chances of a collision.
You help prevent traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: You increase your chances of a collision.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass, your risk of a collision increases.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs affect your driving ability. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, cough syrups, cold tablets, allergy medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Complete your turn only when the intersection is clear and signals allow.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for situations ahead. This sign tells drivers to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: Before you return to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing is allowed, watch your rearview mirror. You can only return to your original lane when you see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass cautiously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm out, it is picking up or dropping off students. You must stop completely. Do not drive until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes in. Never pass a school bus when it is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic go first. You must also always let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, your following distance should be:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, your car takes longer to stop. Keep a greater distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely for any pedestrian or vehicle already in a crosswalk. Only proceed if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings when they obey traffic signals. Drivers must stop for pedestrians at marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It causes the driver to worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and attention.
It draws the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and attention.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous. It uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even good drivers have a higher crash risk when using a cell phone.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes poor decisions and slows your reaction time. You could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a constant speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you come to a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warning devices or flaggers alert you. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass when crossing the centerline in hills, curves, or anywhere you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, where there is a solid yellow line next to your lane, when stopped for a pedestrian, or in construction zones where passing is unsafe.
